text: A psalm of David. LORD, who may dwell in your tent? Who may live on your holy mountain?
The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right, who speaks the truth from the heart;
who spreads no slander with his tongue, who does his neighbor no harm and casts no reproach on his kinsman;

versions.text: who spreads no slander with his tongue, who does his neighbor no harm and casts no reproach on his friend;
versions.explanation: Hebrew קָרוֹב means one who is near — a relative or close neighbor — rather than 'friend' specifically. 'Kinsman' preserves the distinction from רֵעֵהוּ ('neighbor') earlier in the verse and keeps the parallelism intact.

text: who looks with contempt on a vile person but honors those who fear the LORD; who keeps his oath even when it costs him, and does not go back on it;

versions.text: who looks with contempt on the vile but honors those who fear the LORD; who keeps his oath even when it costs him, and does not go back on it;
versions.explanation: 'The vile' as a bare substantive is slightly abstract for oral reading; 'a vile person' matches the Hebrew's focus on an individual (נִבְזֶה ... נִמְאָס) and reads more naturally aloud.

text: who lends his money without interest and takes no bribe against the innocent. Whoever does these things will never be shaken.
